frequency_question: What proportion of major U.S. tariff policy announcements with a pre-set implementation window of 90 days or less successfully complete all required administrative and legal execution steps on or before the target date?
membership_rule: Includes executive orders or proclamation-based tariff rate changes announced with a defined future effective date within 90 days. Excludes legislative tariff changes requiring congressional votes.

cases.name: Liberation Day Tariffs / Universal Baseline Proposal Tests (Historical Simulation)

coverage_note: 5 named major tariff implementation windows under 90 days; believed representative of executive trade action velocity.
known_gaps: Does not fully capture unique complexities of integrated cross-border automotive supply chains, though procedural speed remains bounded by executive authority.
skeleton: Executive actions utilizing emergency powers (IEEPA or Section 232/301) vs standard administrative rulemaking timelines multiplied by required inter-agency clearance steps.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 historical instances where the timeline was under 90 days
validity_reason: Statutory authorities governing presidential tariff implementation (Trade Expansion Act of 1962, Trade Act of 1974, and IEEPA) remain stable across this timeframe.
